text:
ana: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about splitting auth/authorization from query execution for console dashboards. idea: keep query executors lean/stateless, push RBAC checks to a dedicated auth layer that returns a short allow-mask token.

mike: do you mean an edge auth proxy or a per-host sidecar? sidecar avoids one network hop but increases host complexity.

shiv: sidecar likely wins p99 but is annoying operationally. if we do sidecar we need strict upgrade ordering and health hooks so runtime and sidecar don't diverge.

dalia: hybrid thought — do heavy graph traversal at the edge (deny most) and issue a signed allow-mask that runtime can verify cheaply. that keeps fanout fast and cached.

ana: exactly. sketch:
```
edge/auth-proxy -> validate authn, compute allow-mask, sign with KMS
headers: x-allow-mask: base64(...)
         x-allow-sig: <sig>
node: fast verify(sig) && apply(mask) -> short-circuit denied branches
```
Pros: smaller runtime codepaths, better cache hit rates. Cons: extra signing work, TTL/revocation complexity, more telemetry to track mask effectiveness.

mike: benchmark needed: mask compute cost vs per-route graph check. also how mask granularity maps to caching keys — we can't explode cache cardinality.

shiv: revocation story matters. suggest TTL on masks (short, e.g., 30s) + a revocation topic to bump caches for critical permission changes. also add a fallback mode where nodes can re-run full auth if mask validation fails.

jules: ops/telemetry: we need metrics for auth.mode (mask|node), mask_cache_hit, mask_verify_latency, and a counter for fallback_to_node_check. otherwise hard to debug regressions.

deploy-bot: Canary launched: auth-proxy v0.3 on eng-platform/us-west (5 pods), traffic split 2%.

dalia: I'll draft the RFC addendum with config examples, rollout plan, and telemetry dashboard. will include example circuit-breaker rules for when edge/auth-proxy is unhealthy.

ana: thanks — tagging @mike @shiv for review. sync tomorrow 10:00 to agree on canary gates and performance targets.
